Unless conditions require the use of the exact solution, approximate equations are preferable because they are easier to apply and provide greater physical insight. If a calculation (ignoring water autoionization) of the ionization of a weak acid gives a concentration of H3O1 smaller than 1026 m or if a calculation of base ionization gives a concentration of OH2 smaller than 1026 m, then we have to use the more exact treatment. For buffer solutions, a pH near 7 does not necessarily mean that water ionization is important, unless the acid or base concentration becomes very small.

HCN is a very weak acid, but it is nonetheless an acid, not a base.
